blocks.text: I can interpret and construct Punnett squares to show the inheritance of alleles of a single gene.
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: A model used to show the inheritance of alleles from parents to offspring.
A sex cell (sperm or egg) that carries half the genetic information required for an individual organism.
The combination of alleles that an individual has for each gene.
Shows how much of one value there is compared to another.
A measure of the chance or likelihood of an event occurring.
Having two identical alleles for a gene.
Having two different alleles for a gene.

blocks.text: Gametes contain half of the chromosomes of the parent. The resulting zygote has two copies of each chromosome, so it has two copies of each gene, which form a pair.
An individual always has **two alleles for each gene**: one from each parent. Dominant alleles have a capital letter and recessive alleles a lowercase letter.
Most characteristics are influenced by many genes, but some are determined by just one. Punnett squares model a single gene.
The genotype for one gene could be two of the same allele or two different alleles.
Hetero means different. Homo means the same.

blocks.q: Is each genotype homozygous or heterozygous?

blocks.text: When gametes are made, each gamete receives one of each pair of chromosomes, so it receives one allele of each gene.
Mother genotype **ee**: every egg receives an e allele.
Father genotype **Ee**: half of the sperm receive E and half receive e.
A gamete has only ONE allele for the gene, never two.

slides.title: How to build a Punnett square

blocks.text: A Punnett square shows all the possible combinations of genotypes in the offspring, from the alleles in the parents' gametes.

items: Put one parent's two alleles across the top and the other parent's two alleles down the side.
Cross them: in each box, combine the allele from the top with the allele from the side.
Read the possible offspring genotypes from the four boxes.

blocks.text: It does not matter which parent goes on which side.
One parent is heterozygous (Ee) and the other is homozygous recessive (ee). Tap to build each box: allele from the top + allele from the side.
The four boxes are Ee, ee, Ee, ee. So there are two possible genotypes: 2 boxes Ee (heterozygous) and 2 boxes ee (homozygous recessive).
A single gene A codes for a colour pigment in a flower. One parent is homozygous dominant (AA) and the other is homozygous recessive (aa).

blocks.label: What do you notice?
blocks.text: Every box is Aa, so all of the possible offspring are heterozygous.
Two heterozygous parents. Each has E and e to pass on.
Out of four boxes: one EE (homozygous dominant), two Ee (heterozygous) and one ee (homozygous recessive). That is three possible genotypes.
This does NOT mean the parents will have exactly four offspring. The boxes show the possible combinations and the proportions they occur in.

blocks.q: A student draws a Punnett square for Ee × ee and one box says EE. Why must this be an error?
options: Because the ee parent has no E allele to pass on, so no offspring can get two E alleles
Because EE is not a real genotype
Because a Punnett square never has more than one genotype in it
blocks.why: Gametes carry only the alleles their parent has. An ee parent can only pass on e, so an offspring cannot be EE.

blocks.q: Which set of boxes is correct for Aa × Aa?
options: One AA, two Aa and one aa
blocks.why: Each parent passes on A or a, giving AA, Aa, Aa and aa.

blocks.q: Match each cross to the offspring genotypes it can produce.

blocks.text: A Punnett square can be used to predict the likely proportion of each genotype and phenotype in the offspring.
Back to Ee × ee (E = wet earwax is dominant). Ee has a dominant allele so it shows the dominant phenotype. ee has two recessive alleles so it shows the recessive phenotype.
As a ratio: Ee : ee = 2 : 2, which simplifies to **1 : 1**.
Purple (P) is dominant and white (p) is recessive. A PP plant crossed with a pp plant gives 100% Pp, all with purple flowers.
Now cross two heterozygous purple plants, Pp × Pp: the boxes are PP, Pp, Pp and pp.

blocks.label: Why 3 : 1?
blocks.text: Three of the four boxes (PP, Pp and Pp) contain a dominant allele, so they are purple. Only pp is white. As a percentage that is 75% purple and 25% white.
In pea plants, round peas are produced by a dominant allele (R) and wrinkled peas by a recessive allele (r).

blocks.q: Work out each Punnett square, then choose the answer.

items.q: Rr × Rr: what fraction of the offspring are rr (wrinkled)?
Rr × rr: what percentage of the offspring are wrinkled?
RR × rr: what percentage of the offspring are round?
Rr × Rr: what is the ratio of round : wrinkled offspring?
RR × Rr: what percentage of the offspring are RR?

slides.title: Every time is a new chance

blocks.text: Each instance of sexual reproduction is independent, so it does not affect the probability for the next offspring. The ratio and probability stay the same every time fertilisation takes place.

blocks.q: Two Rr pea plants are crossed and their first three offspring are all round. What is the probability that the fourth offspring is wrinkled?
options: 0%, because they have had three round
100%, because it is now wrinkled's turn
blocks.why: Each fertilisation is independent, so the probability of rr stays at 1 in 4 (25%) every time.

items: An individual inherits two alleles for each gene. The alleles may be dominant or recessive.
A Punnett square models the inheritance of alleles from the parents' gametes. It shows all the possible offspring genotypes: homozygous dominant, homozygous recessive or heterozygous.
Punnett squares are used to predict the proportion of genotypes and phenotypes, and the probability of each occurring in the offspring.
Each instance of sexual reproduction is independent, so it does not affect the probability for the next offspring.

flashcards.back: A model used to show the inheritance of alleles from parents to offspring.
A sex cell (sperm or egg) that carries half the genetic information required for an individual organism.

flashcards.front: How many alleles of a gene does one gamete carry?

flashcards.back: Two of the same allele for a gene, e.g. BB (homozygous dominant) or bb (homozygous recessive).
Two different alleles for a gene, e.g. Bb.

flashcards.front: What does a Punnett square show?
flashcards.back: All the possible combinations of genotypes in the offspring, from the alleles in the parents' gametes.

flashcards.front: What offspring do AA × aa parents produce?
What are the possible offspring of Ee × ee, and in what proportions?
flashcards.back: Half Ee and half ee: a 1 : 1 ratio (50% each).

flashcards.front: What is the genotype ratio from two heterozygous parents (Pp × Pp)?
What is the phenotype ratio from two heterozygous parents when one allele is dominant?
flashcards.back: 3 : 1, dominant to recessive, because three of the four boxes contain a dominant allele.
It shows how much of one value there is compared to another.

flashcards.front: Do the ratios change each time a pair of parents has an offspring?
flashcards.back: No. Each instance of sexual reproduction is independent, so the probability stays the same each time.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Models of single-gene inheritance: Punnett squares
worksheet.instructions: Work out each Punnett square, then write a short answer.

questions.prompt: Wet earwax (E) is dominant to dry earwax (e). A heterozygous parent (Ee) and a homozygous recessive parent (ee) have offspring. What percentage of their possible offspring are ee?
questions.explanation: Ee × ee gives two Ee boxes and two ee boxes, so 2 out of 4 is 50%.

questions.prompt: Two heterozygous pea plants (Pp) are crossed. What percentage of the possible offspring have the genotype pp?
questions.explanation: Pp × Pp gives PP, Pp, Pp and pp, so 1 out of 4 is 25%.

questions.prompt: A homozygous dominant plant (AA) is crossed with a homozygous recessive plant (aa). What percentage of the possible offspring are heterozygous?
questions.explanation: Every box of the Punnett square is Aa, so all of the possible offspring are heterozygous.

questions.prompt: Two heterozygous parents (Ee × Ee) are crossed. How many of the four Punnett square boxes show a heterozygous genotype?
questions.explanation: The boxes are EE, Ee, Ee and ee, so two of them are Ee.

questions.prompt: Round peas (R) are dominant to wrinkled peas (r). Two Rr plants are crossed. Write the ratio of round : wrinkled offspring in the form ? : ?
questions.explanation: RR, Rr and Rr are round and rr is wrinkled, so the ratio is 3 : 1.

questions.prompt: Two Ff parents are crossed. Write the genotype ratio FF : Ff : ff in the form ? : ? : ?
questions.explanation: The boxes are FF, Ff, Ff and ff, so the ratio is 1 : 2 : 1.

questions.prompt: What word describes a genotype that has two different alleles for a gene?
questions.explanation: Hetero means different, so two different alleles is heterozygous.

questions.prompt: Two Rr pea plants are crossed and their first four offspring are all round. What is the percentage probability that the fifth offspring is wrinkled?
questions.explanation: Each fertilisation is independent, so the chance of rr is always 1 in 4, which is 25%.

questions.prompt: An organism's body cells contain 36 chromosomes. How many chromosomes does one of its gametes carry?
questions.explanation: Gametes carry half the chromosomes of the parent's body cells: 36 ÷ 2 = 18.

questions.prompt: Round peas (R) are dominant to wrinkled peas (r). A round pea plant (Rr) is crossed with a wrinkled pea plant. What percentage of the possible offspring are wrinkled?
questions.explanation: Rr × rr gives two Rr boxes and two rr boxes, so half are wrinkled (rr).
